subject: Meteorology
title: Weather Radar in Aviation
description: A quick, practical guide to Weather Radar in Aviation.

hook.text: Airborne weather radar lets pilots see thunderstorms ahead—painting precipitation returns on a cockpit display.

buildup.text: Colors indicate intensity—green for light rain, yellow for moderate, red for heavy, and magenta for extreme.

discovery.text: Pilots use radar to navigate around convective cells—threading between storms when possible.

twist.text: Radar has blind spots—it can't see behind heavy cells, and attenuation can hide the worst storms behind closer ones.

climax.text: Ground-based NEXRAD provides broader coverage—ATC uses it to vector aircraft around dangerous weather areas.

punchline.text: Red on the radar means 'go around'—not through.

quiz.question: What does a red return on airborne weather radar indicate?
